content.comment_body: Good afternoon, I'm working with a [product_name] module powered by 24 VDC, which controls 2...10 V damper actuators from [company_name], powered by 24 VAC. During commissioning, I noticed the actuator did not respond to the analog output from the [product_name] unit. I had the electrician link the 0 V terminal of the 24 VAC transformer to the M terminal of the 24 VDC supply for the [product_name], and this resolved the issue. Now, I'm curious about the internal electrical relationship between the M (supply), M1, and M2 (reference for analog outputs). Are these terminals internally connected via a common rail? Thank you in advance.

I haven't heard of a 2...10 V component before, and since no one else replied, perhaps it's a rare setup. It's recommended that all parts and sensors for [product_name] use a common ground for power supply. For outputs, this isn't necessary. The [product_name] provides two outputs for 0...10 V (or 0...20 mA current). The actuator should have a passive 0...10 V input. An active 1...10 V input would not be compatible with the [product_name]. Based on your description, it sounds like your 2...10 V input is active, in which case you cannot use it with the [product_name], unfortunately. [user_name]

I'm a bit confused—was the original question answered? Also, is the focus on the 2–10 V range relevant to the main issue? The 0–1 V portion isn't used. I've worked with equipment from another manufacturer using that range. Variants are also available for 4–20 mA and 1–5 V signals. Using 2–10 V is not particularly uncommon.

analysis.insight_summary: The user encountered a wiring issue when connecting a 2–10 V damper actuator powered by 24 VAC to the analog output of a [product_name] module. This was resolved after tying the 0 V of the AC transformer to the M terminal of the 24 VDC supply. The user seeks clarification on the internal connection between M, M1, and M2 terminals in the [product_name]. Other users expressed confusion about the importance of the 2–10 V signal range in addressing the original issue.
analysis.user_expectations: The user wants detailed information about the internal electrical connections between M, M1, and M2 terminals of the [product_name] unit to ensure correct and safe wiring.
